text:
Although losing out to Trump in the 2016 Republican presidential primaries, Graham became a key supporter of Trump's agenda in the Senate(Image: Getty)

Donald Trump has paid tribute to "one of the greatest people and Senators" after South Carolina Senator Lindsey Graham died from a 'sudden illness.'

The close Trump ally passed away on Saturday evening, his office confirmed in a statement. Writing on Truth Social, Trump paid tribute to Graham saying: "Senator Lindsey Graham, one of the greatest people and Senators I have ever known, is dead! He was always working, and was a true American Patriot. Lindsey will be greatly missed!!! DETAILS AND ARRANGEMENTS TO FOLLOW. So sad!"

Graham had been a fixture of the Republican Party since entering politics in 1994, initially as a Representative before becoming a senator in 2002. Police scanner audio obtained by NBC News revealed that emergency responders were dispatched to his Washington DC residence on Saturday night following reports of a "cardiac arrest" at the property. This comes after Trump was ridiculed over 'diaper' speculation after fleeing the U.S. post-World Cup humiliation.

"On the evening of Saturday, July 11, U.S. Senator Lindsey Graham passed away from a brief and sudden illness," the statement from his office read. "Senator Graham's family appreciates prayers at this time and asks for privacy during this incredibly difficult period."

He had been set to appear on NBC News' Meet The Press on Sunday. Eyewitnesses near his residence when emergency personnel arrived captured images showing paramedics transporting someone on a stretcher to an awaiting ambulance.

Despite challenging Donald Trump for the 2016 Republican presidential nomination, Graham became a devoted supporter of the MAGA movement after his defeat. Speaking at a tele-rally for Graham last month, Trump said: "He's outstanding. He's been at my side for a long time."

Graham was a close ally to Donald Trump(Image: Getty)

Referencing the 2016 contest, the president added: "After that fight was over, we were best of friends, and he's helped me as much as anybody in the Senate."

Graham was a frequent presence in Trump's inner circle, regularly joining the US president on the golf course and speaking with him often. He was particularly influential in advising the president on foreign policy issues including Iran and Russia, and had just announced an agreement on Friday with the Trump administration to advance a package of Russia sanctions.

During his time as a US House member in the 1990s, Graham championed policies designed to isolate the country and curtail its missile and nuclear capabilities. He also voiced strong support for Trump's decision to strike nuclear sites last year and had been a backer of the latest conflict that began several months ago.

Graham held the position of chairman of the Senate Budget Committee and had been pursuing a fifth Senate term in November.

Tributes have started flooding in from across the political spectrum. South Carolina Governor Henry McMaster took to X to honor Graham, calling him an "irreplaceable" political figure.

"The fiercest of fighters for South Carolina and America - and a loyal and steadfast friend," he wrote. "We grieve with Darline [Graham's sister], his family and his devoted staff. May God hold him gently in the palm of his hand. We shall not see his likes again."

It comes after Trump's aide shared an embarrassing video of the president with viewers asking if he needs a 'diaper change'.
